newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds steady after see-sawing on US NAPM.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds steady after see-sawing on US NAPM.

text.p: Irish governments bonds steadied to below Monday's levels in thin afternoon trade on Tuesday after see-sawing with U.S. Treasuries following the release of lower-than-expected NAPM data, dealers said.

"Trade has been reasonable for most of the day. We saw a small recovery on morning levels after the U.S. NAPM data, but then we saw a drop back again to around Monday's closing figures," one dealer said.
At 1520 GMT the eight percent bond due 2001 was down ten pence at 103.45 to yield 6.88. The eight percent bond due 2006 was up two pence at 102.57 to yield 7.48.
Dealers said the domestic market focus still centred on Thursday's Irish private sector credit data for July which is forecast to accelerate by between 13.0 and 13.9 percent.

"To a large extent, high credit figures for July have already been factored into the market, so unless they're really sky-high, we shouldn't have the same market panic we had after the June figures came out," one dealer said.
The Irish end-August Exchequer Borrowing Requirement (EBR), released earlier today, totalled 85 million Irish pounds compared to 524 million in August 1995.
